The standout moment came when I finally got the settings just right, and the search results were spot on. But, I did encounter some frustrating moments when the API would return inconsistent results or fail to index certain pages. Overall, Firecrawl's search API feels like a powerful tool that's still finding its footing. With some patience and experimentation, it can deliver impressive results, but it's not a plug-and-play solution just yet.
top_products.who_should_use: Developers building AI-powered search applications, particularly those in the e-commerce or research spaces, will find Firecrawl's search API to be a valuable tool. However, those looking for a simple, out-of-the-box solution or with limited technical expertise might find it overwhelming.

top_products.what_it_lacks: Prosed lacks a robust editing interface, the ability to export in editable formats, and more control over the layout and design of the book. It also doesn't have any built-in proofreading or fact-checking features, which would be a big plus.
top_products.ai_leverage: While Prosed is built on top of AI models, it's clear that there's some real engineering going on here - the AI is doing more than just simple formatting, it's actually understanding the content and making suggestions. That being said, I think it's possible to rebuild or beat this with today's AI models, especially if you're just looking for a simple formatting tool. However, the value that Prosed adds is in its ease of use and the specific features it's developed to support self-publishing.
